## Trace: classic `z.string().transform(fn)` → core

**1. Public builder and representation.** The builder is declared on `ZodType` as  
`transform<NewOut>(...) => ZodPipe<this, ZodTransform<Awaited<NewOut>, core.output<this>>>`  
— `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/schemas.ts:131-133`. Its runtime implementation is simply:

```ts
transform(tx) {
  return pipe(this, transform(tx));
}
```

— `classic/schemas.ts:245-246`.

The classic `transform(fn)` factory then creates a `ZodTransform` whose def is `{ type: "transform", transform: fn }` — `classic/schemas.ts:2291-2298`. `ZodTransform` extends `core.$ZodTransformInternals<O, I>` / `core.$ZodTransform<O, I>` — `classic/schemas.ts:2243-2249`. Its constructor calls `core.$ZodTransform.init(inst, def)` and `ZodType.init(inst, def)` — `classic/schemas.ts:2249-2255`. The core counterpart is `$ZodTransform` at `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:3820-3839` (`$ZodTransformDef` at 3824, internals at 3828, interface at 3833, constructor at 3837).

The classic `pipe(in_, out)` factory creates `new ZodPipe({ type: "pipe", in: in_, out: out })` — `classic/schemas.ts:2555-2566`. `ZodPipe` extends `core.$ZodPipe` — `classic/schemas.ts:2538-2545` — and its constructor calls `core.$ZodPipe.init(inst, def)`, `ZodType.init(inst, def)`, then exposes `inst.in = def.in` and `inst.out = def.out` — `classic/schemas.ts:2546-2553`. The core counterpart is `$ZodPipe` at `core/schemas.ts:4397-4425` (def at 4401, internals at 4411, interface at 4421, constructor at 4425). The core string schema is `$ZodString` at `core/schemas.ts:367-402` (def at 371, internals at 377, interface at 395, constructor at 399).

**2. Order of input parsing and transformation.** The builder produces a pipe whose `in` is the original string schema and whose `out` is the transform schema. `ZodPipe` does **not** install its own `_zod.parse` in the classic constructor (`classic/schemas.ts:2546-255
